strengths: The paper identifies a timely and practically relevant property of MoE LLMs, local routing consistency, and connects it clearly to expert offloading and cache effectiveness.

The proposed SRP and SCH metrics are well motivated: SRP gives an architecture/model analysis view, while SCH is closer to cache-constrained deployment. The paper also provides derivations showing how the optimal segment decisions can be computed.
The empirical coverage is unusually broad, spanning 20 MoE models with diverse sizes, routing designs, shared expert settings, encoder-decoder and decoder-only architectures, and multiple domains.

The results are informative and actionable: models with MoE in every layer and no shared experts tend to have higher consistency; domain-specialized experts appear more important than vocabulary-specialized ones; and cache size around 2x active experts is a useful rule of thumb for many models.

The appendices improve reproducibility and credibility with architecture tables, data construction details, post-training comparisons, SRP/SCH correlations, confidence intervals, layer-level analyses, and discussion of position effects.
weaknesses: The paper is primarily correlational. Claims about architectural causes, such as shared experts or skipped MoE layers weakening local routing consistency, are plausible but not established by controlled ablations or matched model comparisons.

SCH is an oracle upper-bound metric that assumes knowledge of expert activations within a segment. Although the paper reports correlations with LRU/LFU/fixed cache hit rates, it does not evaluate end-to-end expert offloading systems, latency, memory movement, or quality/speed tradeoffs in realistic decoding deployments.

The practical recommendation that cache size around 2x active experts balances effectiveness and efficiency is somewhat under-supported: it is derived from hit-rate curves rather than actual system cost models, and may vary with hardware, expert size, batching, generation length, and CPU/GPU transfer behavior.

The evaluation corpus uses fixed 512-token samples and mostly analyzes routing over static input sequences. This may not fully capture long-context generation, multi-turn decoding, batch serving, or distribution shifts where expert offloading is most operationally important.

Some metric choices deserve more scrutiny. SRP uses F1 and unrestricted segment routing size, then introduces a size ratio as a secondary metric; alternative formulations such as mutual information, entropy/rank concentration, or cost-weighted hit metrics could change conclusions.

The paper would be stronger with direct comparisons to existing expert prediction/offloading methods beyond cache-hit correlations, and with experiments showing whether high local routing consistency actually preserves model quality or improves wall-clock inference under concrete cache policies.
